name: Motor-Driven Cycle
description: A light motorcycle, motor scooters and motorized bicycles included, with an engine under 150 cc or a motor of five brake horsepower (3,730 W) or less; an electric two-wheeler too fast or powerful to be a moped but within that limit lands here. Defined by Wyoming Statutes §31-5-102(a)(xxiii).
restrictions: A motorcycle: a seat or saddle and no more than three wheels
Its motor produces five brake horsepower (3,730 W) or less; one over two brake horsepower (1,492 W) or faster than 30 mph, or without pedals, is no longer a moped
Not an electric bicycle or a motorized skateboard
Riders need a class M motorcycle license or endorsement
Riders and passengers under 18 must wear a fastened helmet on public roads
Its headlamp must be on at all times, including in daylight
Registered as a motorcycle with the county treasurer, which requires liability insurance
